records.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Production animation source drawings for the EXACT black-and-cream unique mustelid creature White Paw in reference image 1. Draw an animation key-pose sheet on TRUE TRANSPARENT RGBA, a strict 3 columns x 3 rows grid of equal square cells. One complete separate creature per cell, exactly NINE poses read left-to-right top-to-bottom. Same fixed camera front-left three-quarter view and same character, fur colors, stripe pattern, eye scar, amber eyes, rounded ears, enormous white-tipped curled fluffy tail, white paws, fine dark-teal outline, rich smooth hand-painted fantasy game rendering as reference. No redesign, no clothing, no accessories, no text, no cell frames, no ground, no background. The action: the quadruped rises to stand on TWO HIND LEGS, places BOTH FRONT PAWS ON ITS HIPS, proudly holds this pose and breathes, then later sits back down. All nine drawings must keep the same absolute head size and paw size, same scale and shared ground baseline inside their cells; leave ample space above the starting head for standing. Poses: cell 1 exact original low four-legged crouch; cell 2 rear legs begin taking weight, chest lifts slightly and front paws just leave ground; cell 3 chest rises more and both forearms flex toward its waist; cell 4 halfway upright, haunches lowering under pelvis, front paws moving to hips; cell 5 almost upright and front paws reaching hips; cell 6 completely upright on planted hind paws, BOTH elbows bent outward and BOTH white front paws resting clearly on its hips, original head looking left; cell 7 same upright hands-on-hips pose, chest gently lifted for inhalation; cell 8 same upright hands-on-hips pose, chest relaxed after exhalation, elbows still visible; cell 9 same proud upright pose with a small calm head tilt, ready to lower. Stand like a proud natural cartoon mustelid, with short animal legs and intact animal anatomy. Do NOT turn it into a human, do NOT put paws behind its back or across its chest. Keep head and face as close to reference as possible. Keep entire tail and all body parts inside every cell without clipping or touching cell boundaries. Use a fully TRANSPARENT background. The drawings will be used as real animation source cels, so consistent color, outline, identity, scale, lighting and clear anatomical movement are critical. Avoid repetitive identical crouches: the middle and last cells MUST show a real tall bipedal upright stance.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Production layered animation source for reference beetle. Exact reference character: scarred burgundy spiny beetle leader with three ivory back spikes, enormous cracked ivory mandibles, amber eyes and six short dark burgundy segmented legs. KEEP THE EXACT CAMERA, POSE, SCALE, OUTLINE, LIGHTING, SHELL DETAILS, SCARS, SPIKES AND LEGS FROM THE INPUT. Make ONE complete full character sprite on true transparent RGBA. Change ONLY the two IVORY MANDIBLES at the very front: remove both ivory mandibles entirely and reveal/draw the COMPLETE dark burgundy mouth/throat/chin underneath where their upper roots overlap. A clean full jawless mouth base for layered animation. Reconstruct the small previously hidden mouth area with smooth dark burgundy chitin matching the nearby face and abdominal shading; preserve the angry amber eyes and burgundy triangular face plate. The whole shell, body, original six legs, back spikes, scars and silhouette outside the front jaw area must match the reference as closely as possible. Do not replace the mandibles with fangs, tongues, lips or new appendages. No new spikes. No text, ground, scenery, shadows on a background or extra objects. Entire beetle centered inside a square canvas with transparent margin. The original two mandibles will later be layered over this base and articulated as rigid parts.
